name: Latvian Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Sign language: word stress category inapplicable; only lexicostatistical/comparative refs (Bickford 2005, Mahoney 2018) on Glottolog.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page latv1245 (refs: Bickford 2005; Mahoney 2018; Eberhard et al. 2025) and Wikipedia (en, lv, ru) articles on Latvian Sign Language.
sources.note: Glottolog lists no descriptive (grammar/phonology/sketch) reference; ru.wikipedia's 'Grammar' section is empty; lv/en Wikipedia cover only the manual alphabet, legal status and Mahoney/Power et al. comparisons. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Bethere, Dina. 2023. Latviešu nedzirdīgo zīmju valoda starppersonu saziņā un pētniecībā. In Druviete, Ina (ed.), Valodas prakse: vērojumi un ieteikumi 18, 109-123. Rīga: Latviešu valodas aģentūra.
sources.note: Only first-hand structural sketch of LSL found (by the author of the 2004 grammar). Section 'NZV leksiski gramatiskās uzbūves pārskats' covers sign phonology (handshape, hand position, movement, place; fixation-movement-fixation; 56 handshapes; >=11 movement types), morphology and syntax. Nothing on stress/uzsvars. p. 112: 'Pagaidām latviešu NZV zīmju struktūra nav īpaši pētīta' (LSL sign structure has not yet been specially studied). p. 118: non-manual means (facial expression, body posture, intensity of movement) 'have the same significance in sign language as intonation in oral speech'.

sources.citation: Straupeniece, Daiga, Dina Bethere & Elza Ozola. 2023. Sign language of the deaf people: a study on public understanding. Education. Innovation. Diversity 2(7), 108-114. DOI 10.17770/eid2023.2.7356.
sources.note: Public-attitude survey; one paragraph (p. 111) on LSL sign structure (56 handshapes, places, movement types) citing Bethere 2023, and one on syntax. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Mahoney, Shaina. 2018. Apt to change: A comparison of handshape aperture in Estonian and Latvian Sign Languages. BA thesis, Bryn Mawr College (hdl 10066/20033), 29 pp.
sources.note: Comparative handshape-aperture study over a Swadesh-Woodward list; phonology discussed only as the four parameters and Brentari's prosodic model of handshape features. Nothing on stress or sign-level prominence in LSL.
sources.venue: BA thesis, Bryn Mawr College (hdl 10066/20033), 29 pp

sources.citation: Umbrasko, Solvita & Malgozata Rascevska. 2016. Reliability and validity of Latvian Sign Language Comprehension Test (LSLCT) for deaf and hearing impaired children. Journal of Educational and Social Research 6(2), 237-246. DOI 10.5901/jesr.2016.v6n2p237.
sources.note: Test-development paper; p. 238: 'There has been only study of the grammar of the LSL (Bethere, 2004)'. Nothing on stress or phonology of LSL.
sources.venue: Journal of Educational and Social Research

sources.citation: Latvijas Nedzirdīgo savienība, Zīmju valodas centrs. n.d. Par zīmju valodu (web page, zimjuvaloda.lv).
sources.note: Popular description: manual sign components (rokas forma, rokas stāvoklis, zīmes veidošanas vieta, kustība); non-manual means (sejas mīmika, ķermeņa poza, kustību intensitāte) 'veic intonācijas funkcijas'. Nothing on stress. Gives history of LSL dictionaries (Bariss & Poršs 1962: 3401 signs; LNS 1997/1998 'Latviešu zīmju valodas vārdnīca ABC': 1200 signs).

sources.citation: Bethere, Dina. 2006. Latviešu nedzirdīgo zīmju valodas nozīme nedzirdīgo cilvēku kopienas attīstībā. In Valodu apguve: problēmas un perspektīva V, 84-92. Liepāja: LiePA.

sources.note: The only grammar of LSL ('There has been only study of the grammar of the LSL', Umbrasko & Rascevska 2016); a teaching aid from 1998-2002 research.
